title: Topic 39 | Equation of state of an ideal gas

questions.text: Calculate the number of gas molecules in a volume of 1 cm³ at standard conditions (cm⁻³).
Determine the number of molecules in 1 m³ of oxygen at standard conditions.
The number of molecules in 1 m³ of a gas at standard conditions is determined by...
With modern technology a vacuum of 1 pPa can be achieved. How many gas molecules remain in 1 cm³ of such a vacuum at a temperature of 300 K?
The gas pressure in a vessel of size 2.5 × 4 × 3 m³ is 831 mmHg and the temperature is 27°C. How many molecules are in it?
Determine the number of air molecules in a volume of 1 L at standard conditions.
If a vessel of volume 15 L contains 1.8 · 10²⁴ molecules, what is the temperature (K) of this gas at a pressure of 0.5 MPa?
A gas of volume 0.8 m³ at a temperature of 300 K has a pressure of 2.8 · 10⁵ Pa. What will its temperature be (K) if at a pressure of 3.2 · 10⁵ Pa it occupies a volume of 1.4 m³?
The volume of a gas at a pressure of 7.2 · 10⁵ Pa and a temperature of 288 K is 0.6 m³. At what temperature (K) will the same mass of gas occupy a volume of 1.6 m³ if the pressure is 2.25 · 10⁵ Pa?
At a pressure of 6 atm and a temperature of 293 K, a gas occupies a volume of 586 L. Find the volume (L) that the same mass of gas will occupy at a temperature of 248 K and a pressure of 4 atm.
An ideal gas of volume 8 liters at a temperature of 900 K exerts a pressure of 1.5 atm. What must the temperature (°C) of this gas be for its pressure to be 1 atm in a volume of 4 liters?

The diameter of an air bubble rising from the bottom of a body of water to the surface increased 1.5 times. The temperature at the bottom is 5°C and at the surface 27°C. How deep is the body of water, in meters?
How does the pressure of an ideal gas change if its volume and absolute temperature are both increased 2 times?
If, when the gas temperature was raised by 300 K, the pressure and volume each increased 2 times, what is the final temperature of the gas (in kelvins)?

A sounding balloon is filled with gas at a temperature of 27°C to a pressure of 105 kPa. After the balloon rises to an altitude where the pressure is 80 kPa, its volume has increased by 5%. Find the temperature at that altitude (K).
When the absolute temperature of an ideal gas increased 2 times, its pressure increased by 25%. How many times does the volume change?
A rubber boat was inflated at a temperature of 7°C to a working pressure of 108 kPa. Is there a danger of the boat bursting when the temperature reaches 37°C?
answers: Depends on the mass of the boat

questions.text: A thin-walled rubber ball of radius 2 cm contains air at a pressure of 0.1 MPa and a temperature of 20°C. What will the radius of the ball be (cm) if it is lowered to a depth of 20 m in a lake at a temperature of 4°C?
How does the pressure of an ideal gas change if its temperature increases 4 times and its volume increases 2 times?
How did the density of an ideal gas change if its pressure increased 1.5 times when its absolute temperature increased 3 times?
